records.literal_gloss: And answered Bildad the Shuhite and said:

en.L: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:

es.L: Y respondió Bildad el suhita y dijo:

fr.L: Et Bildad le Shouhite répondit et dit :
fr.R: Alors Bildad le Shouhite a dit :

vi.L: Binh-đát người Su-ách đáp lời và nói:
vi.B: Bấy giờ Binh-đát người Su-ách đáp:

ko.L: 그러자 수아 사람 빌닷이 대답하여 말했다.

pt.L: E Bildade, o suíta, respondeu e disse:

decisions.choice: Bildad the Shuhite: the second of Job's three friends, speaking for the third and last time
decisions.reason: Bildad spoke in chapters 8 and 18 (on "Shuhite" see 8:1). This is his third speech, and it is very short, only five verses. Zophar, who spoke in chapters 11 and 20, has no third speech in the book as it stands.

decisions.choice: answered and said: the usual opening of a speech
decisions.reason: "He answered and said" opens each speech in the dialogue (4:1; 8:1). Bildad answers Job's words in chapters 23 and 24.

decisions.choice: answered (B) / said (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use one English verb for the Hebrew pair, as in the other speech introductions of Job. The introduction stays prose.

decisions.choice: "répondit" (Literal, Balanced), "a dit" (Readable) in the speech introduction
decisions.reason: The introduction is narrative: passé simple at Literal and Balanced, passé composé at Readable. Bildad's speech itself uses the present at every level.

source.text: הַמְשֵׁ֣ל וָפַ֣חַד עִמּ֑וֹ עֹשֶׂ֥ה שָׁ֝ל֗וֹם בִּמְרוֹמָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Dominion and dread [are] with him; [he is] making peace in his heights.

en.L: Dominion and dread [are] with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes peace in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heights.
en.B: Rule and dread belong to God; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes peace in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} high places.
en.R: God rules over all, and everyone stands in fear of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q He brings peace to the heavens above.

es.L: El dominio y el pavor [están] con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hace la paz en {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} alturas.
es.B: El dominio y el temor pertenecen a Dios; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} establece la paz en {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} lugares altos.
es.R: Dios gobierna sobre todo, y todos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tienen temor. \q Trae la paz a los cielos de arriba.

fr.L: La domination et l’effroi [sont] avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fait la paix dans {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} hauteurs.
fr.B: La domination et la terreur appartiennent à Dieu ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} établit la paix dans {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} hauts lieux.
fr.R: Dieu règne sur tout, et chacun {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} craint. \q Il fait régner la paix dans les cieux, là-haut.

sw.L: Mamlaka na utisho [viko] pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}; \q hufanya amani mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} pa juu.
sw.B: Utawala na hofu ni mali ya Mungu; \q {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} huleta amani mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} pa juu.
sw.R: Mungu anatawala juu ya vyote, na kila mtu anamcha. \q Huleta amani katika mbingu za juu.

vi.L: Quyền thống trị và sự kinh hãi [ở] với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lập hòa bình trên các nơi cao của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Quyền cai trị và sự kinh sợ thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lập hòa bình nơi cao của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời cai trị trên muôn vật, và mọi người đều kính sợ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Ngài đem bình an đến các tầng trời trên cao.

ko.L: 통치와 두려움이 그분께 [있으니], \q 그분은 그분의 높은 곳에서 평화를 이루신다.
ko.B: 다스리는 권세와 두려움이 하나님께 있으니, \q 그분은 높은 곳에서 화평을 이루신다.
ko.R: 하나님은 모든 것을 다스리시고 모두가 그분을 두려워한다. \q 그분은 저 위 하늘에 평화를 이루신다.

pt.L: O domínio e o pavor [estão] com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} faz a paz nas {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} alturas.
pt.B: O domínio e o pavor pertencem a Deus; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estabelece a paz nas {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} alturas.
pt.R: Deus governa sobre tudo, e todos têm temor {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}. \q Ele traz paz aos céus lá em cima.

decisions.choice: him: God
decisions.reason: Bildad begins without naming God, but the speech is about him: "his heights", "his troops", "his light" (verse 3), "with God" (verse 4).

decisions.choice: dominion and dread: God's rule and the awe it causes
decisions.reason: The first word (hamshel) means ruling power; the second (pachad) is the dread or terror that power brings on those under it (13:11, where Job speaks of God's dread falling on his friends).

decisions.choice: makes peace in his heights: brings order among the powers of heaven
alternatives: keeps peace among the heavenly beings after defeating rebels among them
decisions.reason: "His heights" are the heavens (16:19; 31:2). To "make peace" there is to keep or impose order among the heavenly powers and the bodies of the sky. Some hear in it the old picture of God subduing rebellious powers (9:13; 26:12), but the verse itself says only that he rules the heights in peace.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced names God in the first line so the reader knows at once whom Bildad is talking about (m1).

decisions.choice: God rules over all, and everyone stands in fear of him ... the heavens above
alternatives: Rule and dread are with him
decisions.reason: Readable unfolds the two nouns into a clause (m2) and says "the heavens above" for "his heights" (m3).

decisions.choice: Bildad's speech is in the plain 해라체 (-다, -겠는가) at every level; of God he says 그분 with -시-
alternatives: 하오체 with "그대", as the friends use to Job
decisions.reason: Bildad never turns to Job in this short speech: he describes God and asks general questions about humankind, which Korean keeps in the plain style; 하오체 is kept for lines a speaker addresses to his hearer.

source.text: הֲיֵ֣שׁ מִ֭סְפָּר לִגְדוּדָ֑יו וְעַל־מִ֝֗י לֹא־יָק֥וּם אוֹרֵֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Is there a number to his troops? And on whom not does rise his light?

en.L: Is there a number to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} troops? \q And on whom does {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} light not rise?
en.B: Can {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} armies be counted? \q On whom does {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} light not rise?
en.R: No one can count {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} armies. \q His light shines on everyone.

es.L: ¿Hay número para {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} tropas? \q ¿Y sobre quién no se levanta {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} luz?
es.B: ¿Pueden contarse {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ejércitos? \q ¿Sobre quién no sale {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} luz?
es.R: Nadie puede contar {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ejércitos. \q Su luz brilla sobre todos.

fr.L: Y a-t-il un nombre à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} troupes ? \q Et sur qui {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} lumière ne se lève-t-elle pas ?
fr.B: Peut-on compter {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} armées ? \q Sur qui {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} lumière ne se lève-t-elle pas ?
fr.R: Personne ne peut compter {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} armées. \q Sa lumière brille sur tous.

sw.L: Je, vikosi {{deity_pronoun:vyake|Vyake}} vina hesabu? \q Na ni juu ya nani nuru {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} haichomozi?
sw.B: Je, majeshi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yanaweza kuhesabika? \q Ni juu ya nani nuru {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} haiangazi?
sw.R: Hakuna awezaye kuhesabu majeshi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \q Nuru yake inamwangazia kila mtu.

vi.L: Đạo binh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có số [đếm] được chăng? \q Và ánh sáng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không mọc lên trên ai?
vi.B: Có thể đếm được các đạo quân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sao? \q Ánh sáng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chẳng chiếu trên ai?
vi.R: Không ai đếm được các đạo quân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Ánh sáng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chiếu trên mọi người.

ko.L: 그분의 군대에 수가 있겠는가? \q 그분의 빛이 떠오르지 않는 자가 누구인가?
ko.B: 그분의 군대를 헤아릴 수 있겠는가? \q 그분의 빛이 누구에겐들 비치지 않겠는가?
ko.R: 아무도 그분의 군대를 셀 수 없다. \q 그분의 빛은 모든 사람을 비춘다.

pt.L: Há número para as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} tropas? \q E sobre quem não se levanta a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} luz?
pt.B: Quem pode contar os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} exércitos? \q Sobre quem a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} luz não nasce?
pt.R: Ninguém consegue contar os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} exércitos. \q A luz {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} brilha sobre todos.

decisions.choice: troops: bands of soldiers, here the armies of heaven
decisions.reason: The word (gedud) means a raiding band or troop of soldiers (19:12). God's troops are the hosts of heaven: the heavenly beings, and the stars, which the Bible pictures as an army (Isaiah 40:26). Their numberless size shows God's greatness.

decisions.choice: his light: God's light, like the sun that rises on all
decisions.reason: The light that "rises" is pictured as sunlight. No one is outside its reach; so no one can hide from God or stand apart from him (compare Psalm 19:7).

decisions.choice: two questions that expect the answer "no" and "no one"
decisions.reason: Both questions are rhetorical: there is no counting God's troops, and there is no one his light does not reach.

decisions.choice: statements in place of questions
alternatives: Is there any number to his armies? On whom does his light not rise?
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the questions expect (m3), which is easier for a new reader to follow.

source.text: וּמַה־יִּצְדַּ֣ק אֱנ֣וֹשׁ עִם־אֵ֑ל וּמַה־יִּ֝זְכֶּ֗ה יְל֣וּד אִשָּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And how will be righteous a mortal with God? And how will be pure [one] born of a woman?

en.L: And how can a mortal be righteous with God? \q And how can [one] born of a woman be pure?
en.B: How then can a mortal be righteous before God? \q How can one born of a woman be pure?
en.R: So how can any human being be righteous before God? \q How can anyone born of a woman be pure?

es.L: ¿Y cómo puede un mortal ser justo con Dios? \q ¿Y cómo puede ser puro [el] nacido de mujer?
es.B: ¿Cómo, pues, puede un mortal ser justo delante de Dios? \q ¿Cómo puede ser puro el nacido de mujer?
es.R: Entonces, ¿cómo puede un ser humano ser justo delante de Dios? \q ¿Cómo puede ser puro alguien nacido de mujer?

fr.L: Et comment un mortel serait-il juste avec Dieu ? \q Et comment [celui qui est] né d’une femme serait-il pur ?
fr.B: Comment donc un mortel serait-il juste devant Dieu ? \q Comment celui qui est né d’une femme serait-il pur ?
fr.R: Alors comment un être humain pourrait-il être juste devant Dieu ? \q Comment quelqu’un né d’une femme pourrait-il être pur ?

sw.L: Basi mwanadamu awezaje kuwa mwadilifu pamoja na Mungu? \q Na [yeye] aliyezaliwa na mwanamke awezaje kuwa safi?
sw.B: Basi mwanadamu awezaje kuwa mwadilifu mbele za Mungu? \q Awezaje aliyezaliwa na mwanamke kuwa safi?
sw.R: Kwa hiyo, mwanadamu yeyote awezaje kuwa mwadilifu mbele za Mungu? \q Mtu yeyote aliyezaliwa na mwanamke awezaje kuwa safi?

vi.L: Và làm sao người phàm có thể công chính với Đức Chúa Trời? \q Và làm sao [kẻ] do người nữ sinh ra có thể thanh sạch?
vi.B: Vậy làm sao người phàm có thể công chính trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời? \q Làm sao người do đàn bà sinh ra có thể trong sạch?
vi.R: Vậy làm sao con người có thể công chính trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời? \q Làm sao ai đó do người mẹ sinh ra có thể trong sạch?

ko.L: 그런즉 사람이 어찌 하나님과 함께 의로울 수 있으며, \q 여자에게서 난 [자가] 어찌 깨끗할 수 있겠는가?
ko.B: 그러니 사람이 어떻게 하나님 앞에서 의로울 수 있겠는가? \q 여자에게서 난 자가 어떻게 깨끗할 수 있겠는가?
ko.R: 그러니 어떤 사람이 하나님 앞에서 의로울 수 있겠는가? \q 여자에게서 태어난 사람 가운데 누가 깨끗할 수 있겠는가?

pt.L: E como pode o mortal ser justo com Deus? \q E como pode ser puro [quem é] nascido de mulher?
pt.B: Como pode, então, um mortal ser justo diante de Deus? \q Como pode ser puro quem nasceu de mulher?
pt.R: Então, como pode um ser humano ser justo diante de Deus? \q Como pode ser puro alguém que nasceu de uma mulher?

decisions.choice: Bildad repeats a question already asked in the dialogue
decisions.reason: Eliphaz's vision asked, "Can a mortal be righteous before God?" (4:17), and he repeated it (15:14). Job himself asked, "How can a mortal be righteous with God?" (9:2), meaning he could not win a case against God. Bildad now uses the same words to say that no human being is in the right before God.

decisions.choice: a mortal: a frail human being
decisions.reason: The word ('enosh) stresses human weakness (4:17; 9:2). It means any person, not a man as opposed to a woman.

decisions.choice: born of a woman: any human being, in human weakness
decisions.reason: Job used the phrase in 14:1 and Eliphaz in 15:14. Being born of a woman means sharing the frailty of every human.

decisions.choice: before God
decisions.reason: "With God" here means in God's presence, as one party in a case stands before a judge. Balanced and Readable say "before God"; Literal keeps "with".

source.text: הֵ֣ן עַד־יָ֭רֵחַ וְלֹ֣א יַאֲהִ֑יל וְ֝כוֹכָבִ֗ים לֹא־זַכּ֥וּ בְעֵינָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, even to the moon, and not it is bright; and the stars not are pure in his eyes.

en.L: Look, even the moon, it is not bright, \q and the stars are not pure in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes;
en.B: Look, even the moon is not bright, \q and the stars are not pure in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sight;
en.R: Even the moon is not bright to God, \q and the stars are not pure in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sight.

es.L: He aquí, aun la luna, no es brillante, \q y las estrellas no son puras a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ojos;
es.B: Mira, aun la luna no es brillante, \q y las estrellas no son puras ante {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vista;
es.R: Aun la luna no es brillante para Dios, \q y las estrellas no son puras ante {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ojos.

fr.L: Voici, même la lune, elle n’est pas brillante, \q et les étoiles ne sont pas pures à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} yeux ;
fr.B: Vois, même la lune n’est pas brillante, \q et les étoiles ne sont pas pures à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} yeux ;
fr.R: Même la lune n’a pas d’éclat pour Dieu, \q et les étoiles ne sont pas pures à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} yeux.

sw.L: Tazama, hata mwezi, hauna mng'ao, \q na nyota si safi machoni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}};
sw.B: Tazama, hata mwezi haung'ai, \q na nyota si safi machoni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}};
sw.R: Hata mwezi hauna mng'ao mbele za Mungu, \q na nyota si safi machoni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}}.

vi.L: Kìa, ngay cả mặt trăng, nó cũng không sáng, \q và các ngôi sao không thanh sạch trước mắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}};
vi.B: Kìa, ngay cả mặt trăng cũng không sáng tỏ, \q và các vì sao chẳng tinh sạch trước mắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}};
vi.R: Ngay cả mặt trăng cũng không sáng đối với Đức Chúa Trời, \q và các ngôi sao không trong sạch trước mắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 보라, 달조차도 밝지 않고, \q 별들도 그분의 눈에는 깨끗하지 않은데,
ko.B: 보라, 달조차 밝지 못하고 \q 별들도 그분 보시기에 깨끗하지 않은데,
ko.R: 하나님께는 달조차 밝지 않다. \q 별들도 그분 보시기에 깨끗하지 않다.

pt.L: Eis que nem mesmo a lua, ela não brilha, \q e as estrelas não são puras aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} olhos;
pt.B: Veja: nem mesmo a lua é brilhante, \q e as estrelas não são puras aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} olhos;
pt.R: Para Deus, nem mesmo a lua é brilhante, \q e as estrelas não são puras aos olhos {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.

decisions.choice: even the moon: the moon is the first example in a comparison that ends in verse 6
decisions.reason: "Even to the moon" (hen 'ad yareach) means "take even the moon": if the brightest lights of the night sky are not clean in God's eyes, how much less a human (verse 6). The sentence runs on into the next verse.

decisions.choice: is not bright: does not shine clear
decisions.reason: The verb (ya'ahil) is found only here. It is taken from a root meaning to shine (the related verb in 29:3 and 31:26). Spelled almost the same, a verb for pitching a tent would give "the moon does not pitch its tent", which fits the line less well.

decisions.choice: the stars not pure: compared with God's purity, not morally guilty
decisions.reason: The same argument from the greater to the lesser was made in 4:18 (God does not trust his servants) and 15:15 (the heavens are not clean in his sight). The point is not that the moon and stars are sinful but that nothing created is pure beside God.

decisions.choice: to God
decisions.reason: Readable adds "to God" in the first line, because the Hebrew's "in his eyes" at the end of the verse governs both lines. Readable also ends the verse with a full stop and begins verse 6 as a new sentence.

records.literal_gloss: How much less a mortal, a maggot, and a son of humankind, a worm!

en.L: How much less a mortal, a maggot, \q and a son of man, a worm!
en.B: How much less a mortal, who is a maggot, \q a human being, who is a worm!
en.R: So a human being is far less pure. We are only maggots; \q we are only worms.

es.L: ¡Cuánto menos un mortal, un gusano, \q y un hijo de hombre, una lombriz!
es.B: ¡Cuánto menos un mortal, que es un gusano, \q un ser humano, que es una lombriz!
es.R: Así que el ser humano es mucho menos puro. No somos más que gusanos; \q no somos más que lombrices.

fr.L: Combien moins un mortel, une larve, \q et un fils d’homme, un ver !
fr.B: Combien moins un mortel, qui n’est qu’une larve, \q un être humain, qui n’est qu’un ver !
fr.R: Un être humain est donc bien moins pur encore. Nous ne sommes que des larves ; \q nous ne sommes que des vers.

sw.L: Sembuse mwanadamu, aliye funza, \q na mwana wa binadamu, aliye mnyoo!
sw.B: Sembuse mwanadamu, ambaye ni funza, \q binadamu, ambaye ni mnyoo!
sw.R: Basi mwanadamu hana usafi hata kidogo. Sisi ni funza tu; \q sisi ni minyoo tu.

vi.L: Huống chi người phàm, [là] con giòi, \q và con của loài người, [là] con sâu!
vi.B: Huống chi người phàm, chỉ là con giòi, \q con người, chỉ là con sâu!
vi.R: Thế thì con người còn kém trong sạch hơn nhiều. Chúng ta chỉ là giòi bọ; \q chúng ta chỉ là sâu bọ.

ko.L: 하물며 구더기인 사람, \q 벌레인 사람의 아들이랴!
ko.B: 하물며 구더기 같은 인간, \q 벌레 같은 사람이야 오죽하랴!
ko.R: 그러니 사람은 그보다 훨씬 깨끗하지 못하다. 우리는 구더기일 뿐이다. \q 우리는 벌레일 뿐이다.

pt.L: quanto menos o mortal, um verme, \q e o filho de homem, uma larva!
pt.B: quanto menos o mortal, que é um verme, \q o ser humano, que é uma larva!
pt.R: Então o ser humano é muito menos puro. Não passamos de vermes; \q não passamos de larvas.

decisions.choice: how much less: the conclusion from the greater to the lesser
decisions.reason: The words ('af ki) draw the conclusion from verse 5: if even the moon and stars are not pure before God, how much less a human. Eliphaz argued the same way in 4:19 and 15:16.

decisions.choice: maggot, worm: what is small, low and lives off decay
decisions.reason: The two words appear together in 17:14 and 21:26 ("the maggot covers them"), where they belong to the grave. Bildad uses them for what a human being is in God's sight: lowly, frail and bound for decay.

decisions.choice: a son of humankind: a human being
decisions.reason: "Son of adam" is a Hebrew way of saying one member of humankind (Psalm 8:5, where it stands beside 'enosh as here). It means any human being, man or woman.

decisions.choice: a son of man
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase "son of man" in its traditional English form, as in Psalm 8:5. Balanced and Readable say "a human being" (m3); the phrase here has nothing to do with the title "Son of Man" of Daniel 7 and the Gospels.

decisions.choice: We are only maggots; we are only worms.
alternatives: How much less a mortal, a maggot
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the conclusion of verse 5 and then gives the two pictures as plain statements with "we", so they read clearly as about all people (m3).

decisions.choice: o filho de homem (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase, without the article before "homem" and in lowercase, so it cannot be read as the title "o Filho do Homem" of the Gospels; it means any human being (m3), which Balanced and Readable say. Of the two words for maggot and worm (m2), the first is "verme", as at 17:14 and 24:20, and the second "larva", so the pair stays two words.
